name: graph-immediately-queryable
body:
The graph must be immediately queryable after a completed mutation. Once a mutation returns, any subsequent read by a new process sees the post-mutation state — with no re-scan, no explicit flush, and no session-end step. The acceptance scenario is, verbatim:

    add requirement "foo"
    immediately query and find "foo"

i.e. after `apg node add … foo` returns, an immediate `apg query` (a new process) returns `foo` — with no re-scan, no explicit flush, and no session-end step.

This requirement ROOTS the immediate-queryability contract. Its children `write-through-projection`, `read-your-writes`, `read-access-during-session`, and `commit-then-project` refine it, and it contains the existing `metadata-mutation-graph-consistency` tree (`no-rescan-for-metadata`, `planned-node-removal-reflected`, `projection-delta-atomic`, `rescan-only-on-code-change`, `projection-equals-sources`) so the "immediately queryable" and "no re-scan + exact projection" work read as one tree.
